mainTopic: קריאת שמע על המטה, the value of Torah, and the meaning of יסורין
overview: This עמוד finishes the discussion of קריאת שמע על המטה. A תלמיד חכם is exempt, but אביי says even he must say one verse of mercy. רבי שמעון בן לקיש gives a four-step ladder for beating the יצר הרע. He also teaches that all of Torah, both תורה שבכתב and תורה שבעל פה, was given to משה at סיני. רבי יצחק says bedtime קריאת שמע is like a double-edged sword and keeps מזיקין away. Then the גמרא turns to suffering. Neglecting Torah when you could learn brings יסורין. A suffering person should check his deeds, then check for בטול תורה, and if neither fits, it is יסורין של אהבה. Suffering cleanses sins, and through it ישראל received three gifts: תורה, ארץ ישראל and עולם הבא. A new ברייתא about תורה and גמילות חסדים begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם is exempt from bedtime קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The end of the previous statement: a תלמיד חכם does not need to say קריאת שמע על המטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is a Torah scholar, he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a statement begun on the previous עמוד. It says that a תלמיד חכם does not need to say קריאת שמע על המטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule said everyone should say שמע in bed, even after saying it in shul. This line makes an exception for a תלמיד חכם. He is always learning, so he falls asleep surrounded by Torah, and that already protects him.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is the tail of a statement that started on the previous עמוד. It is not a brand-new topic. 'Does not need to' refers to saying קריאת שמע על המטה.

phrases.english: If he is a Torah scholar —
he does not need to (recite Shema on his bed).
phrases.notes: His constant Torah study protects him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the previous עמוד's discussion of קריאת שמע על המטה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם is exempt from saying קריאת שמע על המטה.

steps.title: אביי: even a scholar must say one verse of prayer
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits the exemption: even a תלמיד חכם must say at least one verse asking for mercy before sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even a Torah scholar needs to say one verse of mercy, such as 'Into Your hand I entrust my spirit; You have redeemed me, ה׳, God of truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows the exemption from Step 1. The scholar may skip the full שמע, but he still has to say one prayerful verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption is not complete. Torah study covers the protection that שמע gives, but a person still needs a moment of asking for mercy before sleep. The model verse, בידך אפקיד רוחי, entrusts one's soul to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Into Your hand I entrust my spirit (תהלים ל״א:ו׳)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for including בידך אפקיד רוחי in the bedtime שמע that is said today.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even a Torah scholar needs
to say one verse of mercy,
such as: 'Into Your hand I entrust my spirit,
You have redeemed me, Lord, God of truth.'
phrases.notes: תהלים ל״א:ו׳

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies and limits the exemption in Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a תלמיד חכם must say at least one verse of mercy before sleep.
steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם is exempt from the full קריאת שמע על המטה, but he must still say at least one prayerful verse, such as בידך אפקיד רוחי.

steps.title: Always stir the good inclination against the evil one
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש teaches that a person should always rouse his יצר טוב to fight his יצר הרע, based on 'רגזו ואל תחטאו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: A person should always stir up his good inclination against his evil inclination, as it says, 'Tremble (be stirred up) and do not sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. It connects to the same verse from תהלים, רגזו ואל תחטאו, that was used for bedtime שמע. The teaching says a person must actively fight his יצר הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רגזו is read as 'stir up' your יצר טוב, not just 'tremble.' The verse means: stir up your good side, and then you will not sin. This opening line sets up the four-step ladder that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He should stir up / rouse to battle
Tremble and do not sin (תהלים ד׳:ה׳)

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama said,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
A person should always stir up
his good inclination against his evil inclination,
as it is said: 'Tremble and do not sin.'
phrases.notes: רגזו = stir up (your good inclination).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: לְעוֹלָם יַרְגִּיז אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side topic linked by the shared verse רגזו ואל תחטאו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must always rouse his יצר טוב to fight his יצר הרע.

steps.title: The ladder: Torah, then קריאת שמע, then remembering death
steps.stepSummary: If stirring up the יצר טוב does not work, a person should learn Torah. If that fails, he should say קריאת שמע. If that fails, he should remember the day of death. Each step comes from the next words of the same verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he beats it, good. If not, he should learn Torah, as it says 'Say in your heart.' If he beats it, good. If not, he should say קריאת שמע, as it says 'upon your bed.' If he beats it, good. If not, he should remember the day of death, as it says 'and be silent, Selah.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן לקיש continues his teaching with a series of backup plans. Each one is stronger than the last, and each is hinted at in the next phrase of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Say in your heart' hints at Torah study. 'Upon your bed' hints at קריאת שמע, which is said when lying down. 'Be silent, Selah' hints at the silence of death. Each tool hits harder than the one before, and the last resort is facing one's own mortality.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four escalating tools against the יצר הרע: (1) stir up the יצר טוב, (2) learn Torah, (3) say קריאת שמע, and (4) remember the day of death. Each is drawn from a phrase of תהלים ד׳:ה׳.
steps.confusionAlert: Remembering death is not the first thing to try. It is the last resort, used only when the gentler tools have not worked.

phrases.english: If he defeats it — good,
and if not — he should engage in Torah,
as it is said: 'Say in your heart.'
If he defeats it — good,
and if not — he should recite Shema,
as it is said: 'Upon your bed.'
phrases.notes: קריאת שמע is said 'when you lie down.'

phrases.english: If he defeats it — good,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — יִזְכּוֹר לוֹ יוֹם הַמִּיתָה,
phrases.english: and if not — he should remind himself of the day of death,
as it is said: 'And be silent, Selah.'
phrases.notes: Silence hints at the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same teaching with escalating fallbacks
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the יצר הרע is not beaten, a person should move in order to Torah study, then קריאת שמע, then remembering the day of death.

steps.title: Each word of the לוחות verse is a part of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש reads שמות כ״ד:י״ב word by word. Each word stands for a section of Torah: the Ten Commandments, מקרא, משנה, נביאים and כתובים, and תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא also said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: What is meant by 'I will give you the stone tablets, and the Torah, and the commandment, which I have written, to teach them'? 'Tablets' are the Ten Commandments. 'Torah' is מקרא. 'Commandment' is משנה. 'Which I have written' is נביאים and כתובים. 'To teach them' is תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same pair of חכמים. It explains one verse by matching each of its words to a different part of Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse seems to list extra items beyond the tablets. רבי שמעון בן לקיש reads each extra word as a separate category. In this way the verse covers both תורה שבכתב and תורה שבעל פה, including משנה and תלמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written

phrases.english: And Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama said,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said,
What is meant by that which is written:
'And I will give you the stone tablets
and the Torah and the commandment
which I have written, to teach them.'
phrases.notes: שמות כ״ד:י״ב

phrases.english: 'Tablets' — these are the Ten Commandments,
'Torah' — this is Scripture (the Chumash),
'And the commandment' — this is Mishnah,
'Which I have written' — these are Prophets and Writings,
'To teach them' — this is Talmud,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching by the same chain of authorities, on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each phrase of שמות כ״ד:י״ב refers to a different part of Torah.

steps.title: All of Torah was given to משה at סיני
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion of the reading: every part of Torah, including משנה and תלמוד, was given to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches that all of them were given to משה from סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion that comes out of the word-by-word reading in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since one verse lists all five categories, all of them were included in what was given at סיני. תורה שבעל פה is not a later human addition. Its roots are in the original giving of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Were given to משה from סיני

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a foundational source for the belief that תורה שבעל פה goes back to סיני.
steps.whatToRemember: Every phrase of the לוחות verse stands for a section of Torah. Together they show that both תורה שבכתב and תורה שבעל פה were given to משה at סיני.

phrases.english: This teaches that all of them
were given to Moshe from Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion drawn from Step 5's reading
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All parts of Torah, Written and Oral, were given to משה at סיני.

steps.title: Bedtime קריאת שמע is like holding a double-edged sword
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that whoever says קריאת שמע on his bed is as if he holds a double-edged sword for protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Whoever says קריאת שמע on his bed is as if he holds a double-edged sword in his hand, as it says, 'The high praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of קריאת שמע על המטה. רבי יצחק describes how powerfully it protects a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying שמע in bed protects a person from harm, like a sword that cuts both ways. The proof verse links praising ה׳ with one's mouth to holding a sword. However, it does not yet show that the verse is talking about bedtime, and the next step asks about exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: High praises of God in their throats (תהלים קמ״ט:ו׳)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who recites Shema on his bed,
it is as if he holds a sword
of two edges in his hand.
As it is said: 'High praises of God in their throats
and a double-edged sword in their hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main topic of קריאת שמע על המטה after the side teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying קריאת שמע on one's bed protects like holding a double-edged sword.

steps.title: How does the verse show it is about bedtime?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the verse from תהלים shows that it refers to קריאת שמע in bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the missing link. The verse mentions praise and a sword, but it never mentions a bed or שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a clarifying question, not an attack on רבי יצחק. It wants to know which word or context ties the verse to bedtime שמע. It sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What implies it? / From where is it inferred?

phrases.english: From where is it implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how Step 7's proof verse connects to bedtime
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verse is connected to קריאת שמע על המטה

steps.title: The verse before it mentions their beds
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא (or רב אשי) answers that the verse just before mentions singing 'on their beds,' so the sword verse follows from praise said in bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, and some say רב אשי, said: From the beginning of the passage, as it is written, 'Let the pious exult in glory; let them sing joyously upon their beds.' And right after it is written, 'High praises of God in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the verse in its context. The verse right before it talks about praising ה׳ on one's bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praising ה׳ 'on their beds' is understood as קריאת שמע על המטה. The very next verse describes those same praises as a double-edged sword in their hands. So the sword is the protection that bedtime שמע gives.

keyTerms.meaning: From the beginning of the passage

steps.whatToRemember: The proof comes from context. Since the previous verse says 'they sing upon their beds,' the next verse's 'sword in their hands' describes the protection of קריאת שמע על המטה.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said,
and some say it was Rav Ashi:
From the beginning of the passage,
as it is written: 'Let the pious exult in glory,
let them sing joyously upon their beds.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קמ״ט:ה׳

phrases.english: And it is written after it:
'High praises of God in their throats
and a double-edged sword in their hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: מֵרֵישָׁא דְעִנְיָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse before it speaks of praising ה׳ 'upon their beds,' which links the sword verse to קריאת שמע על המטה.

steps.title: Saying קריאת שמע in bed keeps מזיקין away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that whoever says קריאת שמע on his bed is protected from מזיקין. He brings a verse from איוב as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Anyone who says קריאת שמע on his bed, demons stay away from him. As it says: "And the sons of רשף fly upward (עוף)."
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second teaching from רבי יצחק about קריאת שמע at bedtime. He says it keeps harmful spirits away, and he quotes a verse that the גמרא will decode in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, רבי יצחק said bedtime שמע is like holding a sword. Now he adds that the danger stays away on its own. The verse he quotes is unclear, so the next step explains what its key words mean.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the verse, usually translated 'sparks'. Here it is read as a harmful force.
'Fly'. Here it is read as a hint to Torah.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
phrases.notes: The same רבי יצחק as in Step 7, adding another teaching.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ
phrases.english: Anyone who recites Shema on his bed
demons stay away from him.
As it is stated: "And the sons of reshef fly upward (uf)"
phrases.notes: איוב ה׳:ז׳. The simple meaning is 'sparks fly upward'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע עַל מִטָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from רבי יצחק on the same theme of bedtime קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קריאת שמע on one's bed keeps מזיקין away.

steps.title: Decoding the words עוף and רשף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from other verses that עוף means Torah and רשף means מזיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word עוף means only Torah, as it says: "Will you set your eyes on it? It is gone." And רשף means only demons, as it says: "Wasted by hunger, devoured by רשף and bitter קטב."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two key words in רבי יצחק's verse so we can see how it supports his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עוף is linked to Torah through a verse about something that flies away the moment you look away, the way Torah is quickly forgotten. רשף appears in a list next to קטב מרירי, which חז״ל understand as a demon, so רשף is a demon too. Read together, the verse means that through Torah, such as the words of שמע, demons are lifted away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And ___ means nothing other than ___'. A formula for defining a word in a verse.
'Will you set your eyes on it?' The flying image is connected to Torah.
'Bitter destruction'. חז״ל understand it as the name of a demon.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the verse by its simple meaning, 'sparks fly up'. The גמרא is giving a דרש meaning: Torah (עוף) raises the demons (רשף) away from a person.

phrases.english: And 'uf' means nothing other than Torah,
as it is stated: "Will you set your eyes upon it? It is gone."
phrases.notes: משלי כ״ג:ה׳. Torah slips away quickly, like something that flies off.

phrases.english: And 'reshef' means nothing other than demons,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְזֵי רָעָב וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף וְקֶטֶב מְרִירִי״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: "Wasting of hunger, devouring of reshef, and bitter destruction."
phrases.notes: דברים ל״ב:כ״ד. רשף is listed next to קטב מרירי, a demon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the verse quoted in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's claim that bedtime שמע keeps מזיקין away
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי כ״ג:ה׳ (עוף means Torah) and דברים ל״ב:כ״ד (רשף means מזיקין)

steps.title: Torah study keeps suffering away
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the same verse differently: עוף is Torah and רשף is יסורין. So Torah study keeps suffering away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Anyone who learns Torah, suffering stays away from him. As it says: "And the sons of רשף fly upward." עוף means Torah, as it says: "Will you set your eyes on it? It is gone." And רשף means suffering, as it says: "Wasted by hunger, devoured by רשף."
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש uses the very same verse but says רשף means suffering, not demons. His teaching is that learning Torah protects a person from יסורין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things change from רבי יצחק's reading. The protective act is now any Torah learning, not just bedtime שמע. And רשף is defined as suffering, because in the verse it sits next to 'wasting from hunger', which is a kind of suffering. The meaning of עוף as Torah stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is busy learning Torah
Wasted by hunger. Shows that רשף belongs to the same kind of thing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Anyone who engages in Torah study,
suffering stays away from him,
as it is stated: "And the sons of reshef fly upward."
And 'uf' means nothing other than Torah,
as it is stated: "Will you set your eyes upon it? It is gone."
And 'reshef' means nothing other than suffering,
phrases.notes: This is where his reading differs from רבי יצחק's.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Wasting of hunger, devouring of reshef."
phrases.notes: He quotes only the part of the verse that pairs רשף with hunger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same verse used by רבי יצחק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah study keeps יסורין away.

steps.title: Even schoolchildren already know this
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects that ריש לקיש's teaching needs no hidden reading, because a clear פסוק in שמות already says it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Even young schoolchildren know this! As it says: "If you listen carefully to the voice of ה׳ your God, do what is right in His eyes, listen to His מצוות and keep all His laws, then every illness I placed on Egypt I will not place on you, for I am ה׳ your healer."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש. Why dig a hidden meaning out of an unclear verse in איוב when an open verse in the Torah already teaches the same thing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is not that ריש לקיש is wrong. It is that his reading adds nothing new. A פסוק in חומש, which even beginners learn, already promises that keeping the Torah protects from illness. So the verse in איוב must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But even...'. Opens an objection that something is obvious.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
phrases.english: But even schoolchildren
know this,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיֹּאמֶר אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע לְקוֹל ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
phrases.english: as it is stated: "And He said: If you will surely listen to the voice of the Lord your God,
phrases.notes: שמות ט״ו:כ״ו

phrases.english: and do what is right in His eyes,
and listen to His commandments and keep all His statutes,
every illness that I placed upon Egypt
I will not place upon you,
for I am the Lord your healer."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָא אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's teaching in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of the איוב verse as 'Torah keeps suffering away'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The idea is already stated openly in שמות ט״ו:כ״ו, so reading it into an unclear verse adds nothing new.

steps.title: One who can learn but doesn't will suffer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן offers a new teaching: whoever is able to learn Torah and does not, הקדוש ברוך הוא brings ugly suffering on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: anyone who is able to learn Torah and does not learn, הקדוש ברוך הוא brings on him ugly sufferings that trouble him. As it says: "I was mute and silent, I kept quiet from good, and my pain was stirred up." And 'good' means only Torah, as it says: "For I have given you a good portion, My Torah; do not abandon it."
steps.whatsHappening: After his objection, רבי יוחנן gives the teaching that really is new. Neglecting Torah when you could learn brings suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals a replacement teaching. The open verse in שמות speaks of reward for keeping Torah. רבי יוחנן's new point is the punishment for failing to learn when you had the chance. He proves it from תהלים, where 'silent from good' means silent from Torah, and that silence leads to pain.

keyTerms.meaning: A good portion or acquisition. Refers to the Torah.

steps.confusionAlert: The punishment is for someone who COULD learn and chose not to. It is not for someone who truly had no ability or opportunity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the lesson from 'Torah protects' to 'wasting a chance to learn has consequences'. The word טוב also sets up the next teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כׇּל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: Rather: anyone who is able to engage in Torah study
and does not engage in it,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings upon him
ugly afflictions that trouble him,
as it is stated: "I was mute with silence, I was silent from good,
phrases.notes: תהלים ל״ט:ג׳

phrases.english: and my pain was stirred up."
And 'good' means nothing other than Torah,
as it is stated: "For I have given you a good portion,
phrases.notes: משלי ד׳:ב׳

phrases.english: My Torah, do not abandon it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כׇּל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ עוֹסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן replaces ריש לקיש's obvious point with a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever can learn Torah and does not, הקדוש ברוך הוא brings ugly and troubling suffering upon him.

steps.title: God was happy to give away the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, or רבי חנינא בר פפא, contrasts a human seller, who is sad to part with his item, with הקדוש ברוך הוא, who rejoiced in giving the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא, and some say רבי חנינא בר פפא, said: Come and see how the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא is not like the way of people. Among people, when someone sells an item to his friend, the seller is sad and the buyer is happy. But הקדוש ברוך הוא is not like that. He gave the Torah to ישראל and was happy, as it says: "For I have given you a good portion, My Torah; do not abandon it."
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same verse just quoted, "לקח טוב," a new אמורא teaches how gladly הקדוש ברוך הוא gave us the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לקח suggests a sale. In a normal sale the seller feels the loss. Here the giver calls His own 'merchandise' 'good' and praises it to the buyer, which shows He is happy to give it. This teaching is attached to the previous step because the two share the same verse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And some say'. Introduces a second possible author of the statement.
'Come and see'. Opens a reflective teaching.
The seller is sad and the buyer is happy

steps.whatToRemember: This section moves through several ideas. Bedtime שמע keeps מזיקין away. Torah keeps suffering away. Neglecting Torah when you could learn brings suffering. And הקדוש ברוך הוא gave the Torah with joy.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said, and some say Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that unlike the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.

phrases.aramaic: מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם, אָדָם מוֹכֵר חֵפֶץ לַחֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: The way of flesh and blood: a person sells an item to his fellow,
the seller is sad, and the buyer is happy.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵּן,
phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so:
He gave the Torah to Israel and rejoiced,
as it is stated: "For I have given you a good portion,
phrases.notes: Calling His 'sale' good shows the Giver's joy.

phrases.english: My Torah, do not abandon it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attached through the verse "כי לקח טוב" quoted at the end of Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike a human seller, הקדוש ברוך הוא rejoiced in giving the Torah to ישראל.

steps.title: When suffering comes, check your deeds, then consider neglect of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or רב חסדא, teaches that a suffering person should first examine his actions. If he finds no sin, he should attribute the suffering to בטול תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא, and some say רב חסדא, said: If a person sees suffering coming upon him, he should examine his deeds, as it says: 'Let us search our ways and examine them, and return to ה׳.' If he examined and found nothing, he should attribute it to neglect of Torah study, as it says: 'Happy is the man whom You afflict, ה׳, and teach from Your Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching about how a person should react when suffering comes. It gives the first two stages of a step-by-step self-check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stage one: suffering is usually a signal to do תשובה, so he checks his deeds (from איכה). Stage two: if he finds no matching sin, he should suspect בטול תורה. The פסוק in תהלים links suffering with 'teaching from Your Torah,' meaning the suffering pushes him back to learning.

keyTerms.meaning: He should search and examine carefully
He should attribute it to (literally: hang it on)
Neglect of Torah study, wasting time that could be used for learning

steps.confusionAlert: 'He found nothing' does not mean he is perfect. It means he found no sin that fits this kind of suffering. בטול תורה is listed separately because people often fail to notice it as a sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects back to steps 12-14. Torah keeps suffering away, so missing Torah study is a natural suspect when suffering comes.

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rav Chisda:

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁיִּסּוּרִין בָּאִין עָלָיו —
phrases.english: If a person sees that suffering is coming upon him —
he should examine his deeds,
as it is said: 'Let us search our ways and examine them,
and return to ה׳' (Eichah 3:40).
If he examined and did not find a sin —
he should attribute it to neglect of Torah study,
as it is said: 'Happy is the man whom You afflict, ה׳,
and teach him from Your Torah' (Tehillim 94:12).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from Torah's value and the punishment for not learning to a practical guide for responding to suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suffering person should first examine his deeds. If he finds no sin, he should attribute the suffering to בטול תורה.

steps.title: If neither fits, it is suffering of love
steps.stepSummary: The same teaching continues. If the person also finds no בטול תורה, then the suffering is יסורין של אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he attributed it to neglect of Torah and did not find that either, it is clear that these are sufferings of love, as it says: 'For the one whom ה׳ loves, He rebukes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's teaching reaches its third and final stage. If there is no sin and no בטול תורה, the suffering comes from God's love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is a kind of suffering that is not punishment at all. The פסוק in משלי compares this to a father who corrects the son he loves. Here the suffering is a sign of closeness, not of failure.

keyTerms.meaning: He attributed it (checked whether it was due to Torah neglect)
It is clear, it is certain
Sufferings of love: suffering that comes from God's love, not as punishment

phrases.english: And if he attributed it to Torah neglect and did not find it so —
it is clear that they are sufferings of love,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ״.
phrases.english: as it is said: 'For the one whom ה׳ loves, He rebukes' (Mishlei 3:12).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-stage process that began in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no sin and no בטול תורה can be found, the suffering is יסורין של אהבה.

steps.title: God brings suffering on the one He desires
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא (through רב סחורה and רבא) teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא brings suffering on anyone He takes pleasure in, based on a פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה, who said in the name of רב הונא: Anyone whom הקדוש ברוך הוא desires, He crushes with suffering, as it says: 'And ה׳ desired to crush him with sickness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching that supports the idea of יסורין של אהבה. Suffering can be a sign that God values a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 only said that loving suffering exists. רב הונא makes a broader claim: suffering is a normal pattern for those God desires. The פסוק in ישעיה joins 'desire' (חפץ) directly to 'crushing with sickness' (דכאו החלי).

keyTerms.meaning: Desires him, takes pleasure in him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Sechorah said that Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָפַץ בּוֹ —
phrases.english: Anyone whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires —
He crushes him with suffering,
as it is said: 'And ה׳ desired to crush him with sickness' (Yeshayahu 53:10).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source and a broader statement backing the idea of יסורין של אהבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever הקדוש ברוך הוא desires, He afflicts with suffering.

steps.title: Does this apply even without accepting the suffering with love?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible thought: maybe the suffering counts as a sign of God's desire even if the person does not accept it with love.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think this is true even if he did not accept the suffering with love?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא raises a possible mistaken idea so that the next step can correct it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's statement sounded unconditional, as if all suffering of a desired person is loving. The 'יכול' asks whether the person's attitude matters at all. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (introduces an idea that will be rejected)

phrases.english: One might think: even if he did not accept them with love? —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far רב הונא's unconditional statement reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether suffering counts as a sign of God's desire even when the person does not accept it with love.

steps.title: Like a guilt offering, suffering must be accepted knowingly
steps.stepSummary: The continuation of the same פסוק, 'if his soul makes itself an אשם,' teaches that just as an אשם is brought knowingly, suffering must be accepted knowingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'If his soul makes itself a guilt offering.' Just as a guilt offering is brought with knowledge and consent, so too the suffering must be accepted with knowledge and consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 19. It shows from the next words of the same פסוק that the person must accept the suffering willingly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיה compares the sufferer to a קרבן אשם. An אשם is brought willingly, with full awareness. So suffering only becomes 'loving suffering' when the person accepts it with understanding, not when he resists or resents it.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the source that settles the question)
Just as... so too... (a comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three stages for suffering: check your deeds, then check for בטול תורה, and if neither fits, it is יסורין של אהבה. God brings suffering on those He desires, but it counts as loving suffering only when the person accepts it knowingly, like a קרבן אשם.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'If his soul makes itself a guilt offering' (Yeshayahu 53:10),
just as a guilt offering is brought knowingly,
so too suffering must be accepted knowingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 by reading the rest of רב הונא's פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Suffering counts as a sign of God's desire only if it is accepted knowingly and willingly, like an אשם.

steps.title: The reward for accepting suffering: children and long life
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק in ישעיה continues. Whoever accepts suffering will see children and live a long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he accepts the sufferings, what is his reward? "He will see children, he will lengthen his days."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same פסוק from Step 20. Now it shows the reward for a person who accepts his suffering with love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 used the words 'if his soul makes itself an אשם' to teach that suffering must be accepted knowingly. The next words of the פסוק, 'he will see children, he will lengthen his days,' now tell us what that person receives. The reward is promised only to someone who truly accepts the suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted them (the sufferings, with love)
He will lengthen his days (long life)

phrases.english: And if he accepted them, what is his reward?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the sufferings, accepted with love as Step 20 required.

phrases.english: "He will see children, he will lengthen his days."
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק in ישעיה (53:10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק to give the reward for the acceptance described in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who accepts suffering with love is rewarded with children and long life.

steps.title: An extra reward: his Torah learning will last
steps.stepSummary: On top of children and long life, his Torah learning will stay with him. The proof is the end of the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but his learning will endure in his hand, as it says: "And the desire of ה' will succeed in his hand."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more reward from the last words of the same פסוק. The person's Torah learning will stay with him and succeed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולא עוד אלא' means 'not only that, but also.' The גמרא reads 'חפץ ה'' (the desire of ה') as the Torah, since the Torah shows what ה' wants. So 'it will succeed in his hand' means his Torah learning will stay with him.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also
The desire of ה'. Read here as the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Accepting suffering with love brings three rewards: children, long life, and Torah learning that lasts.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
phrases.notes: Adds a further reward.

phrases.english: his learning endures in his hand,
as it says: "And the desire of the Lord will succeed in his hand."
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the same פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁתַּלְמוּדוֹ מִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reward from the end of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who accepts suffering also merits that his Torah learning endures.

steps.title: First opinion: love-suffering does not stop Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי and רבי אחא בר חנינא disagree. One says יסורין של אהבה are sufferings that do not stop a person from learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי and רבי אחא בר חנינא disagree about this. One said: these are יסורין של אהבה, any suffering that does not cause בטול תורה. As it says: "Happy is the man whom You afflict, ה', and teach from Your Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: A new argument begins about how to define 'suffering of love.' The first opinion says it is suffering that still lets a person learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof פסוק puts two things side by side: 'whom You afflict' and 'teach from Your Torah.' So the suffering that is a 'happy' kind of suffering is the kind where the person can still learn. Suffering that stops learning would not be called יסורין של אהבה under this view.

keyTerms.meaning: One said (we are not told which of the two)

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי
phrases.english: They disagree about it: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi
phrases.notes: Introduces the dispute.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Acha bar Chanina.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: אֵלּוּ הֵם יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה —
phrases.english: One said: these are afflictions of love —
any that do not involve neglect of Torah,
as it says: "Happy is the man whom You afflict, Lord,
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:12

phrases.english: and teach from Your Torah."
phrases.notes: The suffering comes together with Torah learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי וְרַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the rewards to defining which sufferings count as יסורין של אהבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יסורין של אהבה are sufferings that do not cause בטול תורה.

steps.title: Second opinion: love-suffering does not stop תפילה
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says יסורין של אהבה are sufferings that do not stop a person from praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: these are יסורין של אהבה, any suffering that does not cause בטול תפילה. As it says: "Blessed is God, Who has not turned away my prayer, nor His kindness from me."
steps.whatsHappening: The second side of the argument is given. Suffering of love is suffering that still lets a person pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the test is תפילה instead of Torah. The פסוק links God's kindness with not taking away a person's prayer. So suffering that still allows prayer is a sign of God's kindness and love.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not turn away my prayer

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵלּוּ הֵן יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה —
phrases.english: And one said: these are afflictions of love —
any that do not involve neglect of prayer,
as it says: "Blessed is God
phrases.notes: תהלים 66:20

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא הֵסִיר תְּפִלָּתִי וְחַסְדּוֹ מֵאִתִּי״.
phrases.english: Who did not turn away my prayer nor His kindness from me."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵלּוּ הֵן יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing definition in the same dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יסורין של אהבה are sufferings that do not cause בטול תפילה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both kinds are suffering of love
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of transmitters, רבי יוחנן teaches that both kinds of suffering are יסורין של אהבה. This includes even suffering that stops Torah or תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said to them: this is what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן. Both these and those are יסורין של אהבה, as it says: "For the one whom ה' loves, He rebukes."
steps.whatsHappening: A teaching from רבי יוחנן settles the argument. He says that both kinds of suffering count as suffering of love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's פסוק sets no condition. Whoever ה' loves, He rebukes. So even suffering that does stop a person from learning Torah or praying can still be יסורין של אהבה. This widens the category instead of limiting it.
steps.whatToRemember: The final word follows רבי יוחנן. All suffering that comes without sin, even if it stops Torah or תפילה, is יסורין של אהבה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אלו ואלו' here does NOT mean 'both opinions are right.' It means both kinds of suffering count as love: the kind that stops Torah or תפילה and the kind that does not.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, said to them,
phrases.notes: He is speaking to the two disputing Amoraim.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: thus said Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba (my father),
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה הֵן,
phrases.english: both these and those are afflictions of love,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה׳ יוֹכִיחַ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "For whom the Lord loves, He rebukes."
phrases.notes: משלי 3:12. No condition is mentioned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ יִסּוּרִין שֶׁל אַהֲבָה הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute of Steps 23-24 by putting both kinds of suffering into the category.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All suffering that ה' brings out of love counts as יסורין של אהבה, even suffering that causes בטול תורה or בטול תפילה.

steps.title: Then what does 'And from Your Torah You teach him' mean?
steps.stepSummary: If even suffering that stops Torah learning counts as יסורין של אהבה, then the פסוק's phrase 'from Your Torah You teach him' needs a new explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, what does the פסוק mean when it says 'and from Your Torah You teach him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the second half of the פסוק 'אשרי הגבר אשר תיסרנו יה ומתורתך תלמדנו'. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא will reread the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the phrase seemed to say that loving suffering is the kind that still lets a person learn Torah. But רבי יוחנן just said that even suffering which stops Torah is from love. So the phrase can no longer be a condition about Torah learning, and the גמרא asks what it is for.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the verse come to teach? (asking why a phrase is needed)
And from Your Torah You teach him

phrases.english: But then, what does the verse come to teach by saying
'And from Your Torah You teach him'?
phrases.notes: תהלים צד:יב, the end of the פסוק 'אשרי הגבר אשר תיסרנו יה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבי יוחנן's conclusion that both kinds of suffering are יסורין של אהבה. That conclusion leaves the phrase 'ומתורתך תלמדנו' without its earlier meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the phrase 'ומתורתך תלמדנו' if it is not a condition limiting which suffering is from love?

steps.title: Read it as 'You teach us', not 'You teach him'
steps.stepSummary: The word תלמדנו is reread to mean 'You teach us'. The idea that suffering has value is something the Torah itself teaches us.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not read it as 'You teach him'. Read it as 'You teach us'. This very idea, the value of suffering, You teach us from Your Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with an אל תקרי, a different way of reading the same word. The phrase no longer describes the sufferer. It says the Torah teaches all of us how valuable suffering is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters stay the same, but the vowels change from תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ ('teach him') to תְלַמְּדֵנוּ ('teach us'). Now the phrase is not a condition about which suffering is from love. It points to a source in the Torah, which the next step will give.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (it this way), but rather read it another way. A darshan's rereading of a word.
This matter, meaning the value of suffering

steps.confusionAlert: An אל תקרי does not claim the פסוק is spelled wrongly. The written text stays as it is. The rereading adds an extra layer of meaning.

phrases.english: Do not read it as 'You teach him',
but rather as 'You teach us'.
This matter, from Your Torah You teach us.
phrases.notes: 'This matter' is the value of suffering. It cleanses a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase means the Torah teaches us the value of suffering. It is not a condition about the sufferer's ability to learn.

steps.title: The קל וחומר from an עבד's tooth and eye
steps.stepSummary: An עבד goes free when he loses one limb, a tooth or an eye. Suffering that cleanses the whole body surely frees a person, from his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned through a קל וחומר from the tooth and the eye. A tooth or an eye is only one of a person's limbs. Yet if a master knocks one out, the slave goes free because of it. Suffering cleanses a person's entire body, so all the more so it brings freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows where in the Torah we learn the value of suffering. It uses a קל וחומר from the law of an עבד כנעני who goes free when his master damages his שן or עין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small case is damage to one limb, and even that earns the slave freedom. The big case is suffering that affects the whole body. So it must earn something even greater: freedom from sin, which is atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lesser case to a greater case
Tooth and eye. An עבד goes free if his master destroys one of them (שמות כא:כו-כז).

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual 'from Your Torah' source promised in step 27. It shows that the value of suffering has a basis in a Torah law, not only in aggadic ideas.

phrases.english: It is an a fortiori argument from the tooth and the eye.
Just as the tooth and the eye, which are
only one of a person's limbs,
a slave goes out to freedom through them,

phrases.aramaic: יִסּוּרִין שֶׁמְּמָרְקִין כׇּל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם —
phrases.english: then suffering, which cleanses a person's entire body,
how much more so (it brings freedom from sin).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the Torah source that step 27 said the Torah teaches us.
steps.raayaObject: Suffering brings atonement, which is freedom from sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah law that an עבד goes free when his master destroys his שן or עין.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the word 'covenant' appears with salt and with suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this idea matches ריש לקיש. He points out that the word ברית is used both for salt and for suffering, and he brings a פסוק for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the same as what רבי שמעון בן לקיש said. The word 'covenant' is used with salt, and the word 'covenant' is used with suffering. With salt, as it is written, 'Do not leave out the salt of the covenant.' With suffering, as it is written, 'These are the words of the covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש as support for the idea that suffering cleanses. This step only sets up the matching word ברית in two places. The lesson comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש builds a word-link (גזירה שוה style) between two פסוקים that share the word ברית. One is about salt on קרבנות. The other is the closing of the תוכחה, the curses and sufferings in פרשת כי תבוא.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as (the statement of so-and-so)

phrases.english: And this is the same as the teaching of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
'Covenant' is said about salt,
and 'covenant' is said about suffering.
'Covenant' is said about salt, as it is written:
'Do not leave out the salt of the covenant'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ב:יג, about salting every קרבן.

phrases.english: and 'covenant' is said about suffering, as it is written:
'These are the words of the covenant',
phrases.notes: דברים כח:סט, which comes right after the תוכחה (the list of curses).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, matching source for the same idea that suffering cleanses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word ברית links salt and suffering.

steps.title: Like salt sweetens meat, suffering cleanses sins
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש draws the lesson from the shared word. Salt makes meat good to eat, and suffering cleanses all of a person's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the 'covenant' said about salt means that salt sweetens meat, so too the 'covenant' said about suffering means that suffering cleanses all of a person's sins.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש finishes his comparison and states the lesson. Suffering works on a person the way salt works on meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt may sting, but it improves the meat and makes it fit to eat. In the same way, suffering is painful but it purifies a person from all his sins. This matches the קל וחומר of step 28.
steps.whatToRemember: Two sources teach that suffering cleanses a person: the קל וחומר from an עבד's שן ועין, and ריש לקיש's salt comparison.

phrases.english: Just as the 'covenant' said about salt,
salt sweetens the meat,
so too the 'covenant' said about suffering,

phrases.aramaic: יִסּוּרִין מְמָרְקִין כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.english: suffering cleanses all of a person's sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison set up in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suffering cleanses all of a person's sins, just as salt sweetens meat.

steps.title: Three gifts given only through suffering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא gave ישראל three good gifts, all of them only through suffering: תורה, ארץ ישראל, and עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: הקדוש ברוך הוא gave ישראל three good gifts, and He gave all of them only through suffering. They are: the Torah, ארץ ישראל, and the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another positive side of suffering. This step sets up the next part, where the גמרא will bring a פסוק for each of the three gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, suffering was shown to cleanse sins. Here a new point is added: suffering is the doorway to the three greatest gifts ישראל has. The next three steps bring a פסוק proving this for each gift.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
Three good gifts
the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to Israel,
and He did not give any of them
except through suffering.

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הֵן: תּוֹרָה וְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: These are they: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from 'suffering cleanses sin' to a new point: suffering brings the greatest gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה, ארץ ישראל, and עולם הבא were given to ישראל only through suffering.

steps.title: The source that Torah comes through suffering
steps.stepSummary: The first gift, תורה, is proven from a פסוק that puts suffering right next to learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn that תורה comes through suffering? From the פסוק: 'Happy is the man whom You afflict, ה׳, and whom You teach from Your Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the first of the three gifts, תורה. It shows from a פסוק that suffering leads to תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first speaks of ה׳ afflicting a person and then of teaching him תורה. Putting the two side by side shows that suffering is the path to gaining תורה. This is the same פסוק used earlier in step 27, but there it proved that suffering has value. Here it proves that suffering is how a person acquires תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asks for a source)
You afflict him / You bring him suffering

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same פסוק from step 27. Do not think the גמרא is just repeating itself. Earlier the פסוק showed that suffering is good for a person. Now it is used as the source for the first gift, תורה.

phrases.english: Torah, from where do we know it comes through suffering?
As it is said: 'Happy is the man'
whom You afflict, ה׳,
and whom You teach from Your Torah.'
phrases.notes: Suffering and learning תורה appear together in one פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first פסוק proof for the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that תורה is given only through suffering
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים צ״ד:י״ב, 'Happy is the man whom You afflict, ה׳, and whom You teach from Your Torah'

steps.title: The source that ארץ ישראל comes through suffering
steps.stepSummary: The second gift, ארץ ישראל, is proven from two פסוקים next to each other. The first speaks of ה׳ rebuking us, and the next speaks of ה׳ bringing us to a good land.
steps.simpleTranslation: ארץ ישראל: as it is written, 'Just as a man rebukes his son, ה׳ your God rebukes you.' Right after that it is written, 'For ה׳ your God is bringing you to a good land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the second gift, ארץ ישראל. It shows that rebuke and suffering come first, and right after that comes the good land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by order. One פסוק speaks of ה׳ rebuking us like a father rebukes his son. The very next section speaks of ה׳ bringing us into the good land. Because they are placed together, the rebuke is understood as the way to reach ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written after it

phrases.english: Eretz Yisrael, as it is written:
'For just as a man rebukes his son,'
'ה׳ your God rebukes you,'
and it is written right after it:
'For ה׳ your God is bringing you'
'to a good land.'
phrases.notes: The good land comes right after the rebuke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second פסוק proof, following the same pattern as the proof for תורה in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that ארץ ישראל is given only through suffering
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים ח׳:ה׳ and דברים ח׳:ז׳, placed one after the other

steps.title: The source that the World to Come comes through suffering
steps.stepSummary: The third gift, עולם הבא, is proven from a פסוק that calls rebuke and discipline 'the way of life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולם הבא: as it is written, 'For a מצוה is a lamp and תורה is light, and the rebukes of discipline are the way of life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the third gift, עולם הבא. This completes the proofs for all three gifts in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The way of life' is read as the road to the eternal life of עולם הבא. The פסוק says that this road is made of rebuke and discipline. So suffering in this world is what brings a person to עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of life (read here as the path to eternal life)

steps.whatToRemember: All three gifts, תורה, ארץ ישראל and עולם הבא, have a פסוק showing that they come through suffering. Each proof links a word about rebuke or affliction to the gift itself.

phrases.english: The World to Come, as it is written:
'For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light,'
'and the way of life is the rebukes of discipline.'
phrases.notes: The road to eternal life goes through rebuke and suffering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third and final proof, which completes the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that עולם הבא is given only through suffering
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי ו׳:כ״ג, 'and the way of life is the rebukes of discipline'

steps.title: A new teaching about someone who learns Torah and does kindness
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא begins, taught before רבי יוחנן, about a person who is busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים. Its ending continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבי יוחנן: Anyone who is busy with תורה and with acts of kindness...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new teaching. Only the opening appears here, and the rest of the sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new ברייתא, still on the larger topic of suffering. It describes a person who is involved in תורה and in גמילות חסדים. What it says about that person comes on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא taught (a reciter of ברייתות)
One who is busy with / engages in

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not try to find the ruling in this step, because it comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
Anyone who engages in Torah
and in acts of kindness
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs for the three gifts are finished, a new ברייתא opens on the related topic of suffering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Its ruling is not yet given on this עמוד. It concerns a person who engages in תורה and גמילות חסדים, and it continues on the next עמוד.
